newsitem.title: USA: Parkway Holdings may divest noncore assets.
newsitem.headline: Parkway Holdings may divest noncore assets.

text.p: Parkway Holdings Ltd Finance Director Tan Kai Seng said on Wednesday the company will look to streamline operations and divest some of its non-core assets.

Speaking at the Flemings-sponsored Asia '96 Investors Conference in New York, Seng said the Singapore-based regional healthcare holding company "will take active steps to review options over the short term."
"We will be taking a serious look at our non-healthcare assets, and I would expect we should divest some of these assets in the medium term," he said.
He did not provide a time frame for divestitures.
"Our focus is on healthcare. We plan to stay in healthcare," he said. Healthcare contributed about 78 percent of Parkway's 1995 pre-tax profit of Singapore $79.8 million.
Noncore assets include property investments, construction and food manufacturing and distribution.

Seng said Parkway has become the dominant private healthcare provider in Singapore and the surrounding region due to expansion at its flagship Gleneagles Hospitals and the contributions of Mount Elizabeth and East Shore Hospitals, which were acquired in 1995.
Seng said the company expects private healthcare demand in the region to grow strongly as the population becomes increasingly affluent and more highly educated.

Parkway has hospitals in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, India and Sri Lanka. Seng said that while Parkway expects to expand and add beds at some of these locations, it does not expect to expand to other Asian countries in the immediate future.

He said Parkway's hospitals get patients from nations in Asia where the company often does not have operations. "We see an increasing trend of traveling to us for acute treatment," he said. "I think we will focus on this high margin type of treatment over acquisitions" in the immediate future.
